From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents against our playbook. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Key constraint:** No authority has been given by Amelia Frost for the 20% / AUD 4.8m cap or the 18-month claims period. Neither fallback should be offered until she provides written approval identifying the draft.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap

- **Seller position:** Cl 12.1 caps general Warranty Claims at 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
- **Buyer should want:** Opening position of 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The 20% fallback is available only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft, which has not been given.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6m.** The 20% figure is a conditional fallback that is not authorised.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket

- **Seller position:** Cl 12.2 sets a AUD 25,000 de minimis and a AUD 250,000 basket, recovering only the excess above the basket.
- **Buyer should want:** AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 aggregate basket, with the seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; restore 5k / 50k first-dollar.** A deductible-style basket of AUD 250k would remove most realistic claims from recovery.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit

- **Seller position:** Cl 12.3/13 sets 18 months for general claims and applies any limitation to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer should want:** 24 months after Completion. The 18-month fallback needs Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given. The "applies to all Claims" wording is a hidden general-regime override and should be removed.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; counter at 24 months and delete the blanket-override wording.** The override would reach title, fundamental and fraud claims that must sit outside the general regime.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime

- **Seller position:** Capacity and title warranties are subject to the general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer should want:** A separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Folding title and capacity into the general regime would cap and time-bar our most important protections.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out

- **Seller position:** Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature," with no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer should want:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; insert the full carve-out.** The seller draft would protect a seller from claims arising from its own fraud.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope

- **Seller position:** The Disclosure Letter at 1.1 and 1.2 discloses everything in the data room as at 22 Sept 2026, plus the Accounts, statutory registers and public records.
- **Buyer should want:** Specific, fair disclosure only. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject 1.1 and 1.2 entirely.** General deemed disclosure would silently neutralise most warranty claims.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier

- **Seller position:** Cl 8.3 bars any claim for matters the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything "discoverable from the data room or public records."
- **Buyer should want:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier must name seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete 8.3 and replace it with the named-person, reasonable-enquiry qualifier.** "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge bar that would shift diligence risk onto the buyer.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent

- **Seller position:** Cl 3/6.3 uses reasonable endeavours and treats consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. Disclosure item 2 confirms no final consent or evidence of satisfied conditions is included. Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, or ~30%, of FY26 revenue.
- **Buyer should want:** Effective consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion. Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent. Consent-on-delivery is not acceptable.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; make effective Bluefen consent with evidence of satisfied conditions a pre-Completion condition.** Thirty percent of revenue depends on it.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility

- **Seller position:** Cl 2/7 addresses the approximately AUD 3.2m facility with a release "to be provided following Completion." Disclosure item 3 confirms the facility is unpaid and no discharge is included.
- **Buyer should want:** A current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases. A post-completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; require payout from Completion funds and effective releases at Completion.** Leaving a secured AUD 3.2m debt post-Completion exposes the buyer to the security.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses

- **Seller position:** The AUD 420,000 DD-005 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow. Disclosure item 5 says it is unknown whether payroll tax, super or on-costs apply.
- **Buyer should want:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or seller-funded. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Recommendation:** **Require a specific line item or seller funding, including on-costs.** Silent exclusion from the funds flow would leave the buyer funding the payment.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity

- **Seller position:** Cl 11.1 limits the indemnity to the SOW3 payment and calls it adequate. Disclosure item 4 notes the AUD 180,000 is open and no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
- **Buyer should want:** A broader indemnity that preserves the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- **Recommendation:** **Broaden the indemnity and keep the SOW3 cure.** The narrow indemnity does not cover IP transfer risk beyond the disputed fee, and the figure should not be treated as confirmed either way.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)

- **Seller position:** Cl 4.6/Sch 6 calls it preliminary and "not expected to be material." Disclosure item 6 says the scope, unauthorised access and notification duty are not established.
- **Buyer should want:** Preserve logs, investigate and require updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject "not material" as a characterisation; require log preservation, investigation and regular updates, with rights reserved.** Neither side's conclusion is established on the current record.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)

- **Seller position:** The three renewals (AUD 110k each) are ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure item 8 states it is unknown whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer should want:** Assessment of the renewals. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Recommendation:** **Accept the assessment process; reject any automatic debt or price deduction.** The record does not yet support either classification.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation

- **Seller position:** Tax, IP and title issues are all placed under the general regime "above."
- **Buyer should want:** Keep Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories separate. No hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; restore separate categories.** Collapsing them into the general regime would cap and time-limit categories that need their own protection.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification

- **Seller position:** Title to 100% of shares is "evidenced" by the DD-012 share register. Disclosure item 10 says the buyer has not verified title.
- **Buyer should want:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. DD-012 is a seller-supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject DD-012 as sufficient; require independent verification** (for example, ASIC extract, register inspection, PPSR search and authority evidence). A seller-prepared register cannot verify the seller's own title.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms

- **Seller position:** Tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer should want:** Tax and IP terms remain open. Assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject "settled"; keep open and flag for further negotiation.** The general-regime settlement would cap tax and IP exposure that is unresolved.
